{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) when measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation yielded the highest success rate (0.780) and fastest Time-to-Target (2.56s), with strong Path Efficiency (0.502) and Average Speed (12.83), plus the highest AD (0.399)",
    "Bright Visual Only performed comparably to Combined on success (0.785 vs 0.780) and Path Efficiency (0.504), with slightly lower Average Speed (12.68) and AD (0.387)",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only showed intermediate performance: success rates of 0.685 and 0.673, Time-to-Target around 3.05-3.14s, and lower Path Efficiency (~0.43-0.43)",
    "Sham stimulation produced dramatically worse outcomes: lowest success (0.273), slowest Time-to-Target (4.68s), poorest Path Efficiency (0.308), slowest Average Speed (10.74), and lowest AD (0.236)",
    "AD values ranged from 0.236 (Sham) to 0.399 (Combined), suggesting stimulation increases angular dispersion in mouse navigation paths",
    "Sample sizes vary substantially across paradigms: Combined dominates with 48,846 trials (63.7%), while Sham has only 3,505 trials (4.6%) and Bright Visual Only has 3,323 trials (4.3%)"
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Success rate: Sham (0.273) versus Combined/Bright Visual Only (~0.78-0.79) shows a 2.9-fold difference, the largest effect across any variable",
    "Time-to-Target: Sham (4.68s) is 1.83× slower than Combined (2.56s) and 1.79× slower than Bright Visual Only (2.61s)",
    "Path Efficiency: Sham (0.308) versus Combined (0.502) represents a 63% relative deficit",
    "Average Speed: Sham (10.74) is 16.6% slower than Combined (12.83) and 15.7% slower than Bright Visual Only (12.68)",
    "AD: Combined (0.399) versus Sham (0.236) shows a 69% relative increase, with visual-only and ICMS-only conditions intermediate",
    "The gap between Sham and all active stimulation conditions exceeds differences among active stimulation conditions themselves for most variables"
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Any form of stimulation—whether intracortical microstimulation (ICMS), visual cues (dim or bright), or their combination—substantially improves mouse navigation performance compared to no stimulation. The Combined paradigm and Bright Visual Only appear most effective, suggesting that sensory guidance (particularly visual) enhances performance. Notably, Bright Visual Only nearly matches Combined performance despite lacking ICMS, indicating that visual cues may be the primary driver of performance gains. The elevated AD under stimulation suggests more exploratory or varied movement patterns when sensory information is available, which paradoxically correlates with better performance outcomes. Sham conditions produce severely impaired navigation, confirming that stimulation effects are not merely due to task engagement or non-specific arousal.",
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in sample sizes: Combined has 14× more trials than Sham and Bright Visual Only, potentially affecting precision of estimates for smaller groups",
    "No statistical tests (ANOVA, post-hoc comparisons, confidence intervals) provided to assess significance of observed differences",
    "No information on within-mouse variability or whether mice were tested across multiple paradigms (repeated measures) or assigned to single paradigms (between-subjects)",
    "AD interpretation as 'angular dispersion' is assumed from instructions; the metric's precise behavioral meaning is not defined in artifacts",
    "No data on learning effects, trial order, or session effects that could confound paradigm comparisons",
    "Missing information on how 'Success' was operationalized (binary threshold? time limit?)",
    "Path Efficiency shows extremely high maximum value (29.8) suggesting possible outliers or calculation anomalies not addressed"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct mixed-effects regression modeling with Mouse as a random effect to account for clustering of trials within mice and potential cross-paradigm exposure, followed by pairwise comparisons with appropriate multiplicity correction. Examine distributional properties of Path Efficiency given its extreme maximum value. If repeated measures exist, analyze within-mouse paradigm transitions to isolate stimulation effects from individual differences. Visualize group differences using boxplots or violin plots to assess distributional shapes and identify outliers. Finally, model AD as a predictor of Success to test whether higher angular dispersion under stimulation reflects adaptive exploration versus inefficient path selection."
}
